districts.vibe: Office-core CBD — residential is a yield trade, not a lifestyle move.
districts.demographics: Predominantly tenants: foreign professionals in banking, law, consulting. Owner-occupiers are rare and skew SC/PR expats with CBD commutes. Almost no families; studio and 1BR dominant.
districts.tenure_mix: Almost entirely 99-yr leasehold from Marina Bay reclamation releases; a few FH boutique shophouse conversions.
districts.typical_size_range: 450-1,500 sqft (studios to 3BR, with penthouse outliers at Wallich)
districts.psf_range_sgd: S$2,600 – S$3,400 psf (2026 range — CBD private condos)
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Limited new launches; Marina South GLS site and a couple of boutique redevelopments. Net supply tight.
suits: Yield-led investor with CBD office-demand thesis

SC/PR single or couple wanting zero-commute lifestyle

faqs.q: Is D1 a good investment district?
faqs.a: Yields compress to ~3% because entry PSF is high. Best suited to investors with >10yr hold who value CBD office-demand exposure and FX hedging. Not for first-time OOE buyers — poor value-per-sqft versus RCR alternatives.

faqs.q: What's the tenure situation in D1?
faqs.a: Almost all 99-year leasehold from the Marina Bay reclamation era. Freehold is rare and commands a noticeable premium when it surfaces, usually via shophouse conversions.

faqs.q: Best MRT access in D1?
faqs.a: Raffles Place is the NSL+EWL interchange. Shenton Way (TEL, opened 2022) added meaningful connectivity for Marina South. Marina Bay is a triple-line node (NSL+CCL+TEL).

districts.vibe: Walking-distance CBD with real rejuvenation — Newport FH is the 2026 headline.
districts.demographics: Expat professionals + SG singles/DINKs working in CBD. Mixed renter/owner; Wallich sets the ultra-prime tone. Very few families.
districts.tenure_mix: Mix of 99-yr (newer GLS) and FH (Newport, some boutique). Newport's FH status is a core thesis.
districts.psf_range_sgd: S$2,600 – S$3,500 psf (Newport FH premium at upper end)
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Newport Residences launched 2024; absorption ongoing. Limited new GLS here — Cecil Street redevelopments trickle in.
suits: FH-seeking prime buyer (Newport thesis)
CBD-commuting executive owner-occupier
Restructurer looking for trophy unit with long runway

faqs.q: Is Newport Residences worth the premium?
faqs.a: Newport is one of very few FH prime-CBD launches of this decade. Premium over neighbouring 99-yr stock is 15-25%. Worth it only if you value FH and can hold 10+ years — otherwise D1/D2 99-yr gives better yield per dollar.

faqs.q: D1 vs D2 — which is better for investment?
faqs.a: D2 is the cleaner pick right now. Marina view is priced-in for D1; D2 has more redevelopment upside around Cecil Street and benefits from TEL's Maxwell station. Rental tenant pool is similar.

faqs.q: How's connectivity from Tanjong Pagar?
faqs.a: Tanjong Pagar EWL is 1 stop to Raffles Place. Maxwell TEL (2022) added north-south access. Outram Park 3-line interchange is a 7-min walk. Genuinely well-connected.

districts.vibe: City-fringe sweet spot — mature MRT, quality schools, en-bloc-rich. Holds value through cycles.
districts.demographics: Mix of SC families, young PMET couples, and expat renters. Tiong Bahru draws creative/F&B professionals. Queenstown rejuvenation attracting upgraders.
districts.tenure_mix: Predominantly 99-yr; pockets of FH apartments. HDB stock is significant in Queenstown.
districts.psf_range_sgd: S$2,200 – S$2,900 psf (new-launch RCR), resale S$1,800-2,400 psf
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Several GLS sites in Queenstown pipeline; en-bloc pipeline active around Alexandra. Moderate supply, well-absorbed.
suits: HDB upgrader wanting RCR with CCR proximity
Investor seeking balance of yield and capital appreciation
Family wanting schools + city access

faqs.q: Why is D3 considered a sweet spot?
faqs.a: 10 minutes to both Orchard and CBD, mature MRT, strong school catchment, and consistent en-bloc refresh. PSF is ~25-30% below CCR equivalents for similar commute. Best risk-adjusted district in the RCR.

faqs.q: Tiong Bahru vs Queenstown — which to pick?
faqs.a: Tiong Bahru = character, FH boutique pockets, cafe culture, thinner new-launch pipeline. Queenstown = modern, more new launches, better MRT access via TEL. Tiong Bahru for lifestyle, Queenstown for liquidity.

faqs.q: Is Avenue South Residence still a good buy in 2026?
faqs.a: TOP-era depreciation has largely played out. Compare resale PSF against launch PSF — if you're getting in at near-launch, it's reasonable. Greater Southern Waterfront remains a 15-20yr catalyst that isn't yet fully priced.

districts.vibe: Sentosa is a niche FX/foreign-buyer game; HarbourFront mainland is the more practical play.
districts.demographics: Sentosa Cove: foreign UHNW, SC returnees, very low density. HarbourFront mainland: SC/PR professionals, Keppel/VivoCity commuters, some expat renters.
districts.tenure_mix: Sentosa Cove 99-yr; mainland D4 mixed 99-yr with some FH (Caribbean at Keppel Bay etc.).
districts.psf_range_sgd: Sentosa Cove S$1,800-2,500 psf (still below 2013 peak); HarbourFront mainland S$1,900-2,600 psf
districts.yield_range: 2.5% – 3.5% gross (Sentosa thinner; HarbourFront tighter renter demand)
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Very limited. Greater Southern Waterfront masterplan is the decade-long overhang — positive long-term, but no imminent launches.
suits: Foreign UHNW buyer (Sentosa Cove is one of the few SG plots open post-2011 rules)
SC/PR wanting waterfront lifestyle with Keppel Bay views
Long-hold GSW thesis investor

faqs.q: Has Sentosa Cove finally bottomed?
faqs.a: PSF has recovered from the 2013-2020 trough but still trails 2013 peak in many projects. Volume remains thin. Bottom may be in, but liquidity risk is the real issue — exits can take 12-18 months.

faqs.q: Keppel Bay vs Sentosa Cove?
faqs.a: Keppel Bay is mainland, better rental liquidity, more realistic yields. Sentosa Cove is the trophy play — zero commute to CBD (via Sentosa Gateway), but tenant pool thin and MCST costs high.

faqs.q: What's the Greater Southern Waterfront impact?
faqs.a: Keppel Port relocation frees ~1,000 hectares over 15-20 years. Genuinely transformative for D4/D3, but timeline makes it a long-hold bet, not a 5-year play.

districts.vibe: Quietly strong — NUS, one-north, Science Park demand pillars. Tenant-friendly, mature stock.
districts.demographics: Academics, NUS faculty/staff, biotech/tech professionals at one-north, postgrad students. Mix of expat renters and SC owner-occupiers.
districts.tenure_mix: Mix of 99-yr condos and FH apartments; landed FH in West Coast area.
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Clementi GLS sites released; moderate pipeline. Greater Southern Waterfront edge benefits D5 long-term.
suits: Yield-focused investor leveraging NUS/one-north tenant demand
Family buying into Nan Hua / NUS High catchment
HDB upgrader preferring west-side quietness

faqs.q: Why is D5 rental yield higher than neighbouring districts?
faqs.a: Three institutional demand pillars: NUS (staff + postgrads), one-north (biotech/tech), and Science Park (R&D). Tenant base is deep and price-insensitive for mid-tier units. 3.5-4% gross is achievable on the right stack.

faqs.q: Is Normanton Park worth considering in 2026?
faqs.a: 1,862 units — large project with corresponding exit liquidity risk. But the PSF remains reasonable versus one-north proximity. Pick the right stack (east-facing, pool-view, mid-high floor) and it works.

faqs.q: How does Clementi compare to Queenstown (D3)?
faqs.a: Clementi is ~20% cheaper PSF, ~5 min further to CBD, tenant pool is more institutional (NUS/one-north) vs CBD-led in D3. For yield, Clementi wins; for capital growth, D3 has historically led.

districts.vibe: Tiny district by sales volume — mostly old commercial-residential mixed-use.
districts.demographics: Very thin residential pool; mostly singles in boutique city-fringe units. High transient / serviced apartment mix.
districts.tenure_mix: Mix of FH shophouse-resi and 99-yr; very few pure-residential projects.
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Negligible pure-resi pipeline. Any upside is from mixed-use redevelopment (Funan-adjacent sites).
suits: Ultra-niche city-living buyer
Short-term investor trading on serviced-apartment conversion plays

faqs.q: Can you actually live in D6?
faqs.a: Yes, but the residential pool is small. Most buyers pick D1/D2/D9 for city living — D6 is chosen mostly for specific projects like The Clift or boutique shophouse conversions.

faqs.q: Is D6 good for investment?
faqs.a: Thin transaction volume makes valuation harder. Liquidity risk on exit. Not recommended unless the specific project has clear rental story (serviced apartment operator, expat corporate lease).

faqs.q: Why is D6 so small?
faqs.a: Urban-planning history — the City Hall/High Street area was built primarily for commercial and civic uses. Residential is incidental to those zones.

districts.vibe: Gentrifying fast — Guoco Midtown anchor, F&B + creative tenant pool.
districts.demographics: Young professionals, creatives, hospitality workers. Mix of expat and SC renters. Starting to attract DINK owner-occupiers post-Midtown.
districts.tenure_mix: Mixed — Midtown Bay/Modern 99-yr, some FH older stock. Land-scarce.
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Midtown cluster absorption continues; limited fresh GLS. Supply tight.
suits: CBD-adjacent investor who wants character + yield

faqs.q: Is D7 under-rated versus D9?
faqs.a: Yes. D7 is ~15-20% cheaper PSF than D9 for similar commute times to both CBD and Orchard. Guoco Midtown commercial anchor is adding genuine tenant demand. Gap should narrow.

faqs.q: Midtown Bay vs Midtown Modern?
faqs.a: Modern is residential-first with larger family layouts. Bay is smaller, more investor-centric. Modern has the better owner-occupier story; Bay is a yield + lock-up-and-leave play.

faqs.q: How's the rental market in D7?
faqs.a: Deep, driven by F&B, hospitality, creative agency workers, and Raffles Hospital staff. 1BR/2BR rent well. Studios can be softer — too much supply from older conversions.

districts.vibe: Underrated CCR-fringe — yield-friendly, Indian professional + medical tenant base.
districts.demographics: Indian professional expats (Farrer Park Hospital, Mustafa, tech), SC singles, mid-income families in older stock. High rental turnover.
districts.tenure_mix: Mix of FH shophouse conversions and 99-yr newer builds. Kampong Java has some FH apartment blocks.
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Piccadilly Grand absorption nearly done; some GLS in Kampong Java / Jalan Besar watch list.

Restructurer buying for rental liquidity

faqs.q: Why does D8 have better yields than neighbouring districts?
faqs.a: Structural tenant demand from Farrer Park Hospital (medical tourism + staff), Mustafa (24/7 retail workers), and the Indian professional community. Rental market is one of the most liquid in the CCR-fringe.

faqs.q: Is Piccadilly Grand still relevant in 2026?
faqs.a: TOP'd 2024. Rental market has absorbed it well. Resale PSF has held — this is a fairer entry than launch for yield-led buyers.

faqs.q: D7 vs D8 — which for investment?
faqs.a: D7 has higher capital upside (Midtown catalyst). D8 has higher current yield. If holding <7 years, D8 wins on cash-on-cash. Longer holds, D7 likely outperforms on total return.

districts.vibe: Singapore's prime-of-prime — liquidity strong, FX-driven. Quiet luxury beats bling.
districts.demographics: UHNW SC, PR, foreign investors (China, HK, India, Indonesia). Owner-occupier mix heavy at top end; strong rental market for expat C-suite.
districts.tenure_mix: Strong FH stock (Cairnhill, River Valley) balanced with 99-yr Orchard Boulevard precincts.
districts.psf_range_sgd: S$2,800 – S$4,500 psf (Park Nova / Boulevard 88 at upper end; River Valley 99-yr nearer S$2,400)

faqs.q: Is D9 prime worth the PSF premium?
faqs.a: For capital preservation and liquidity in a downturn, yes — prime CCR is the most liquid tier for foreign buyers. For yield, no — D15/D3/D8 deliver better cash. Pick based on portfolio purpose.

faqs.q: FH vs 99-yr in D9?
faqs.a: FH Cairnhill/River Valley still commands 15-25% premium over 99-yr at entry. Over 30+ years the premium compounds as 99-yr decays. For multi-generational holds, FH is correct. For 10-15yr holds, 99-yr offers better yield.

faqs.q: How has ABSD impacted D9 liquidity?
faqs.a: 60% foreign ABSD (from Apr 2023) thinned foreign buying by ~70% at peak. Market has adjusted — PSF held up because supply tightened in parallel. Liquidity on resale is slower; holding periods stretched.

districts.vibe: Family prime — school zones drive premium; landed enclave premium intact.
districts.demographics: SC families (often 2nd/3rd generation), expat C-suite renters, returnees. Heavy owner-occupier skew. Intergenerational wealth visible.
districts.tenure_mix: Heavy FH — Ardmore, Tanglin, Bukit Timah landed. 99-yr only in newer GLS pockets.

faqs.q: Is 1km school catchment still worth paying for?
faqs.a: Yes — distance registration phases still apply (Phase 2C). Top-tier primaries (Nanyang, RGPS, Henry Park) generate measurable PSF premium, particularly on units within 1km radius.

faqs.q: D10 vs D11 for family living?
faqs.a: D10 has deeper top-school catchment and the landed enclave cachet. D11 has better MRT (Novena NSL interchange) and hospital access. D10 is the 'quiet wealth' pick; D11 is more functional.

faqs.q: How are GCBs performing in 2026?
faqs.a: GCB market is SC-only and thin — typically 30-60 transactions a year. Prices have held up post-2023 ABSD changes because buyer pool (SC UHNW) wasn't directly impacted. Long-hold inflation hedge.

districts.vibe: Health corridor — NSC / TTSH / Mt Elizabeth. Family-friendly, MRT-rich.
districts.demographics: Medical professionals, SC families, expat families (medical tourism-adjacent), mid-senior management. Balanced owner/renter.
districts.tenure_mix: Mix of FH (Newton, Watten) and 99-yr (Novena recent launches).
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: Watten House launched 2023; Mount Pleasant GLS (former police site) is a medium-term catalyst.

faqs.q: Why is D11 called the health corridor?
faqs.a: TTSH, National Skin Centre, Mt Elizabeth Novena, Novena Medical Center are all clustered. Rental demand from medical staff, visiting specialists, and medical tourists is structural — underwrites rental liquidity.

faqs.q: D10 vs D11 — which is more liquid?
faqs.a: D11 sells faster, especially 99-yr stock near Novena MRT. D10 FH holds value longer but transactions take longer. D11 for 7-10yr hold, D10 for 15yr+.

faqs.q: How's Mount Pleasant development going?
faqs.a: Former police academy redevelopment is a decade-long project. First GLS parcels expected mid-late 2020s. Adjacent projects (Watten House, upcoming GLS) will benefit — but timeline is patient-capital territory.

districts.vibe: City-fringe HDB-heavy — Toa Payoh en-bloc supply reshapes mid-2030s.
districts.demographics: Heavy HDB owner-occupier base, SC families, older demographics in Balestier. Limited expat renters — mostly Indian professionals near Novena edge.
districts.tenure_mix: Majority HDB; private is mixed 99-yr with some FH apartments in Balestier/Moulmein.
districts.supply_pipeline_2026_2028: The Orie is the headline 2026 launch; further en-bloc opportunities in older Toa Payoh HUDC/private stock over 2027-2030.

faqs.q: Is The Orie worth buying at launch?
faqs.a: Toa Payoh hasn't had a fresh private launch in over a decade. Scarcity premium is real. Compare against Bishan D20 PSF to benchmark — if The Orie prices within 5-8% of Bishan, reasonable. Beyond that, stretch.

faqs.q: Why so little private supply in D12?
faqs.a: HDB land use dominates Toa Payoh. Private GLS releases are rare. This creates supply-scarcity upside when en-bloc deals trigger redevelopment — which is the 2025-2030 thesis.

faqs.q: D12 or D13 for a RCR entry?
faqs.a: D12 has the better schools (CHIJ TP, Maris Stella primary fringe) and city access. D13 is cheaper and has Potong Pasir charm. D12 for families; D13 for yield-led investors.

districts.vibe: Quiet performer — CCL access, affordable RCR for upgraders.

districts.tenure_mix: Majority 99-yr; small FH apartment pockets.

faqs.q: Is Bidadari the long-term winner in D13?
faqs.a: Bidadari masterplan is one of HDB's best-designed new estates. Proximity to Woodleigh MRT + The Woodleigh Residences mall is driving rental demand. Private stock next to Bidadari should compound.

faqs.q: Park Colonial vs The Woodleigh Residences?
faqs.a: Park Colonial has the Woodleigh MRT doorstep. The Woodleigh Residences has the integrated mall + Japanese-developer design. Park Colonial for yield; TWR for lifestyle + resale story.

faqs.q: Why is D13 cheaper than D12?
faqs.a: D12 has Toa Payoh heritage and stronger primary-school catchment. D13's strength is transit (CCL) — improving but not yet priced-in. Expect gap to narrow over the next cycle.

districts.vibe: Two-speed — Geylang FH + Paya Lebar Quarter mature; Ubi industrial-fringe stays niche.

faqs.q: Is Geylang FH stock a value play?
faqs.a: FH walk-ups and strata-landed in Geylang trade at significant discount to CCR FH. Works if you accept the tenant mix and en-bloc timeline patience. Not owner-occupier territory for most.

faqs.q: Park Place Residences at PLQ — worth it in 2026?
faqs.a: Integrated development with mall + MRT is a premium proposition. PSF reflects that. Yield is reasonable on smaller units; capital growth depends on PLQ office occupancy.

faqs.q: When does Paya Lebar Air Base move?
faqs.a: Scheduled for 2030 onwards. Full redevelopment will take decades. Too far out for a 5-10yr thesis, but supports long-hold D14/D17 positioning.

districts.vibe: East Coast lifestyle premium — walkable, cafe-rich, mature schools. New launches priced accordingly.

faqs.q: Is D15 oversupplied in 2026?
faqs.a: Near-term yes — Grand Dunman (1,008 units), Tembusu Grand (638), Continuum (816), plus Tanjong Katong GLS. Absorption will take 24-36 months. Resale may see price pressure until pipeline clears.

faqs.q: Amber vs Marine Parade — which pocket?
faqs.a: Amber is quieter, FH-rich, Katong Park TEL doorstep. Marine Parade is 99-yr new launches, mall-integrated at Marine Parade MRT. Amber for hold-to-pass-on; Marine Parade for rental.

faqs.q: How has TEL opening changed D15?
faqs.a: Meaningfully. East Coast historically rail-poor — buses or drive. TEL cut Orchard/CBD commute by 15+ minutes. Catalyst mostly priced-in by 2024, but resale liquidity is now stronger.

faqs.q: Is Bayshore the next big east-side story?
faqs.a: TEL station + waterfront precinct + new GLS launches = genuine catalyst. But total supply is large. Early movers who pick best-positioned stacks benefit; late buyers at peak pricing face supply pressure.

faqs.q: D15 vs D16 — where's better value?
faqs.a: D15 is more mature, cafe/school premium priced-in. D16 is 15-20% cheaper PSF with Bayshore catalyst ahead. For investors, D16 offers better forward return; for lifestyle, D15 wins today.

faqs.q: How bad is the east oversupply risk?
faqs.a: D15 + D16 combined have 3,500+ units launching/absorbing 2024-2027. Resale market will face competition from new launches. Best to buy at launch pricing or wait for absorption cycle to end.

districts.vibe: Industrial-anchored — aviation + CBP tenant pool. Niche residential.

districts.tenure_mix: Mostly 99-yr condos; landed FH in Jalan Loyang Besar enclave.

faqs.q: Is D17 too far for most buyers?
faqs.a: Yes — commute times to CBD are 30+ minutes. Works only if you/tenant is based in Changi/CBP/Pasir Ris. Not a mainstream upgrader pick.

faqs.q: Does Changi T5 impact D17 prices?
faqs.a: Long-term tailwind, but timeline is mid-2030s. Won't drive 5yr returns. Better to buy on current cash-yield math than future catalyst.

faqs.q: Landed in D17 — worth it?
faqs.a: Jalan Loyang Besar FH landed is cheap vs D10/D11. Trade-off is commute, ambience, resale liquidity. Works for SC families prioritising space over location.

districts.vibe: Mature regional centre — Tampines Hub + retail draw. Pinery Residences is the 2026 anchor.

faqs.q: Why is Pinery Residences significant?
faqs.a: First major new launch in mature Tampines in years. Integrated amenities proximity (Tampines Hub / Mall cluster). Will set PSF benchmark for the district in 2026.

faqs.q: Treasure at Tampines — still a buy?
faqs.a: Mega-development (2,203 units). TOP'd, absorption on resale ongoing. Stack selection matters — pool-facing mid-floor trades at premium. Exit liquidity is the risk given project size.

faqs.q: How does Tampines compare to Punggol for upgrading?
faqs.a: Tampines is mature, schools deeper, retail proven. Punggol is newer, better waterfront, Digital District catalyst. Tampines for stability; Punggol for growth.

districts.vibe: Family-suburban — Punggol Digital District ramping. HDB-upgrader heartland.

faqs.q: Is Punggol Digital District a real catalyst?
faqs.a: Yes — SIT campus operational, JTC offices absorbing fintech/cybersecurity tenants. PSF in adjacent Punggol condos has outperformed broader OCR. Real impact, not speculation.

faqs.q: Hougang vs Serangoon Gardens for landed?
faqs.a: Serangoon Gardens is the established FH landed enclave — higher PSF, mature ambience. Hougang has newer strata-landed at better prices. Gardens for long-hold; Hougang for value.

faqs.q: The Florence Residences worth considering?
faqs.a: Large 1,410-unit project. TOP'd 2023. Resale pricing has stabilised. Kovan MRT proximity is the hook. Good yield for young landlords; appreciation modest given project size.

faqs.q: Why is Bishan HDB resale so expensive?
faqs.a: Catholic High + Raffles Institution catchment, NSL+CCL interchange, mature town. HDB resale in Bishan regularly crosses S$1M for 5-room. Private condo PSF follows that premium.

faqs.q: Is Thomson View en-bloc a buy signal?
faqs.a: En-bloc redevelopment signals land-value confidence. Expect launch PSF at S$2,400-2,700 given Upper Thomson MRT doorstep. Nearby 99-yr stock (Thomson Impressions, Thomson Grand) benefits.

faqs.q: D20 vs D11 for family buyers?
faqs.a: D11 is closer to Orchard, ACS/SJI catchment. D20 has Raffles/Catholic High, better parks (Bishan-AMK), cheaper PSF. D20 is better risk-adjusted family value.

faqs.q: Is The Reserve Residences worth its premium?
faqs.a: Integrated development (mall + MRT + bus interchange) is a structurally scarce proposition. PSF reflects that. For families on HCI/NJC catchment with mid/long hold, it works. Yield-led investors can find better.

faqs.q: How will Pine Grove impact D21?
faqs.a: Pine Grove redevelopment releases substantial new supply. Near-term pressure on resale PSF at neighbouring projects. Long-term, refreshes the district and drives up land-value benchmarks.

faqs.q: D21 vs D10 — which is better for schools?
faqs.a: D10 has the Nanyang Primary + RGPS flagship. D21 has HCI Secondary/JC + NJC. For primary-stage planning, D10. For secondary-stage preparedness, D21 wins.

faqs.q: Is JLD really a second CBD?
faqs.a: URA masterplan commits decades of development. JEM/Westgate/IMM are the anchor retail. New office towers + mixed-use in pipeline. Timeline is 15-25 years for full build-out. Real but patient.

faqs.q: J'den worth the launch PSF?
faqs.a: J'den is on the former JCube site at Jurong East interchange. Premium vs nearby projects reflects integrated + interchange proximity. Works for JLD-thesis long-hold; near-term yield is tight.

faqs.q: When does JRL fully open?
faqs.a: Jurong Region Line phased openings from late 2020s through early 2030s. Full completion adds meaningful connectivity across D22/D23/D24. Prices adjust as each phase opens.

faqs.q: Is D23 too far from the city?
faqs.a: DTL gets you to Bugis in ~30 min, Newton ~25 min. Liveable for most, but not zero-commute. Trade-off is PSF ~25-30% below comparable D15/D16.

faqs.q: Senja Close EC worth considering?
faqs.a: ECs in 2026 come with income ceilings. For income-qualified upgraders, EC remains the highest-value new-launch format. Senja Close specifically — check MOP timeline + completion to decide hold strategy.

faqs.q: D23 vs D24 Tengah for new buyers?
faqs.a: D23 is mature — infra done, schools established. D24 Tengah is brand-new — pricing reflects anticipation. D23 for 'buy and live immediately', D24 for 'patient masterplan upside'.

faqs.q: Is Tengah too early to buy?
faqs.a: Depends on horizon. MRT doesn't open until 2027+, town centre still under construction. 3-year buyers face immature living experience. 10-year buyers capture the masterplan story. Know your hold period.

faqs.q: Tengah Garden Residences — worth launch pricing?
faqs.a: First major private launch in Tengah. Scarcity premium real, but you're paying for a catalyst not yet delivered. If launch PSF >S$2,100, compare hard against Copen Grand resale.

faqs.q: Tengah vs Punggol for new buyers?
faqs.a: Punggol has working infrastructure + PDD catalyst already in motion. Tengah is 3-5yr behind Punggol's current state. Punggol for near-term liveability; Tengah for deeper long-hold discount.

faqs.q: Will RTS actually impact property prices?
faqs.a: Yes — cross-border time drops from 60-90 min (bus) to 5 min (rail). Unlocks MY executive rental pool for D25. But impact is concentrated around Woodlands North specifically, not all of D25.

faqs.q: Is D25 an SAS-catchment play?
faqs.a: Singapore American School is a material rental driver. Expat American families near SAS pay premium for 3BR+ units within 15-min drive. Genuine niche demand.

faqs.q: D25 vs D27 Yishun for affordability?
faqs.a: D25 has RTS catalyst D27 lacks. D27 has better established retail (Northpoint City). D25 for upside bet; D27 for current liveability.

faqs.q: Is Lentor cluster oversupplied?
faqs.a: Likely near-term. 5-7 projects launching within 1km over 2022-2027. Resale liquidity will be thin until absorption completes. Buy at discount to launch, or wait for pipeline to clear.

faqs.q: Lentor Modern vs Lentor Hills Residences?
faqs.a: Lentor Modern has the integrated mall + MRT exit (doorstep). Lentor Hills is further from MRT but larger site with better amenities. Modern for convenience; Hills for space-per-dollar.

faqs.q: How does TEL change D26?
faqs.a: Transformative. Pre-TEL, Lentor was bus-reliant. TEL connects to Orchard in 20 min. PSF pre-TEL was ~S$1,500; current S$2,000+. Much of the uplift is priced-in now.

faqs.q: Is North Park Residences still a buy?

faqs.a: Yishun is more mature (retail, hospital, interchange). Sembawang is quieter, newer, has seaside aspect. Yishun for convenience; Sembawang for ambience at similar PSF.

faqs.q: Sembawang EC 2026 — should I queue?
faqs.a: ECs remain the best-value new-launch format for income-qualified upgraders. Sembawang EC specifically — evaluate commute tolerance + MOP resale strategy. Queue if you fit the income ceiling.

faqs.q: Why is D28 so small in volume?
faqs.a: Predominantly landed enclaves + airbase land. Private condo stock is thin. Not a natural target for upgraders or investors — mostly chosen by existing residents or niche landed buyers.

faqs.q: Is Jalan Kayu / Seletar Hills landed a value play?
faqs.a: Versus D10/D11 landed, yes — significantly cheaper per sqft of land. Trade-off is commute, ambience, resale liquidity. Works for end-use families, not short-hold investors.

faqs.q: When does CRL reach D28?
faqs.a: Cross Island Line phase with Seletar station is on the longer horizon (late 2020s/2030s). Too distant to drive near-term pricing. Worth monitoring for 10-15yr positioning.
